A collection of short films, edits, social media posts, and experiments I’ve directed, edited, and produced for coursework, extracurricular projects, and independent creative exploration. These were all made with a combination of iMovie, Premiere Pro, and Canva.

### Documentary: Halloweekend in Claremont

This short documentary gives a brief, intimate peek into the parties thrown throughout Halloweekend 2024 (Oct 31 - Nov 2). Examining music, design, communication pipelines, and administrative changes at Pomona since the 90’s, we designed this project to include the documentary below and a complementary ethnographic research paper. 

[click here to watch](https://jazzminpearlduncan.github.io/jazz/multi/Halloweekend.html)

### Hi-De-Ho: Honoring Cab Calloway, the Rotoscope, and Animation History
*History*
```{=html}

<div style="text-align: center;">
    <iframe width="640" height="360" 
      src="https://www.youtube.com/embed/Agc6IAtV9MU" 
      frameborder="0" 
      allowfullscreen>
    </iframe>
  </div>

```

This video (and the project it was submitted with) explores how animation can both immortalize and obscure cultural contributions, examining the interplay between adaptation and historical visibility. The video highlights key moments in animation and music history, incorporating stylistic recreations, backtracking, and archival references.

### Visual Album
*Coming Soon: Apple Juice: Music Videos & Black Music Television as Sites of Creative & Extra-cultural Alchemy*

This is my senior thesis project, which explores the creative and cultural possibilities of music videos, visual albums, and music television. I'm researching how music videos can function as more than promotional tools for songs—as audiovisual art forms that transform music, imagery, performance, technology, and cultural memory into something new.

Alongside the written research, I’m developing a seven-minute, seven-part visual album. Each part will explore a research question through formal audiovisual decisions and the creative application of historical processes. Together, the pieces will put the project’s research into practice, using the visual album format as both a subject of study and a medium for experimentation.
